systems.name: Sliding
systems.meta_description: Glaze sliding aluminium window and door systems — precision rollers, sashes to 300 kg, spans to six metres.
systems.schema_description: Precision-engineered aluminium sliding window and door systems with sashes to 300 kg and spans to six metres.
systems.hero_lede: Walls of glass that move with a fingertip — and stand still against everything else.
overview_body: Precision-engineered stainless rollers carry the sash instead of dragging it, so a panel weighing 300 kg moves under one hand. Nothing swings into the room and nothing crowds the view — the pane simply steps aside.
The sliding series run from a modest balcony door to a six-metre glazed elevation. Whichever depth a project needs, the thermally broken core, the German hardware and the tested seal are the same.

strengths.title: Fingertip glide
strengths.copy: Twin stainless rollers on a hardened track. The weight is carried, not dragged — the panel takes the same effort at 60 kg and 300 kg.

strengths.title: Spans to six metres
strengths.copy: The 201 series takes a single sash six metres tall, letting one pane do the work an entire wall used to.

strengths.title: Sealed against weather
strengths.copy: Class 4 air permeability and 600 Pa of water tightness with no leakage — tested to BS EN 12207 and 12208.

strengths.title: Quiet inside
strengths.copy: Rw 41–44 dB across the range. Laminated acoustic glazing brings a main road down to a background murmur.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue, with the series that suit Sliding listed first.
systems.teaser_desc: Walls of glass that glide on precision stainless rails — panoramic openings that move with a fingertip and disappear into the architecture.
systems.enquiry_note: Panels glide past each other on precision tracks — the everyday choice for balconies and living rooms.

variants.lede: One panel parks behind the other — the smallest sliding format.

variants.name: 2 Track · 4 Panel
variants.lede: Four leaves on two rails, clearing from the middle outward.

variants.lede: Full-height glass on twin rollers; half the elevation moves.

variants.name: 3 Track Sliding Door
variants.lede: A third rail stacks all three leaves at one jamb — two thirds open.

variants.name: Slim Sliding Door
variants.lede: The interlock drawn down to a line. Six metres of sash.

variants.name: Sliding Door with Mesh
variants.lede: An insect screen on its own track, in the same frame.

systems.name: Lift & Slide
systems.page_title: Lift & Slide Systems — Glaze Window Systems
systems.meta_description: Glaze lift and slide aluminium doors — sashes to 300 kg, six metres of height, airtight the moment the handle is released.
systems.schema_category: Aluminium lift & slide windows and doors
systems.schema_description: Aluminium lift and slide door systems carrying sashes to 300 kg and six metres of height.
systems.hero_lede: Turn the handle and the panel lifts off its seal. Release it and the whole weight settles back down.
overview_body: The handle raises the sash clear of its gasket before it travels, so a 300 kg panel moves under one hand and the seal is never dragged along its own length. Release the handle and that same weight presses the gasket shut again.
Lift and slide runs on the heavy sliding-door profiles — the series carrying sashes from 120 kg to 300 kg, at heights up to six metres.

strengths.title: Lift, then glide
strengths.copy: The gasket is only under load when the door is closed, so it never wears against the track.

strengths.title: Sashes to 300 kg
strengths.copy: The 201 series carries a 300 kg leaf — a pane most systems would have to split in two.

strengths.title: Six metres tall
strengths.copy: A single sash spans six metres of height, so the opening is set by the architecture rather than the hardware.

strengths.title: Airtight when set
strengths.copy: Dropping the sash compresses the seal on every edge — Class 4 air permeability, 600 Pa water tightness.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue, with the series that suit Lift & Slide listed first.
systems.teaser_desc: Turn the handle and the panel rises from its seal, gliding weightlessly. Release, and it settles back — airtight, silent, secure.
systems.enquiry_note: Panels lift and glide with fingertip effort — for wide, uninterrupted openings onto terraces and views.

systems.name: Bi-Fold
systems.meta_description: Glaze bi-fold aluminium doors — leaves that stack aside to open a whole elevation, with flush thresholds and 150 kg capacity.
systems.schema_description: Aluminium bi-fold door systems that fold an entire elevation into a single stack.
systems.hero_lede: Leaf after leaf stacks aside until nothing at all stands in the opening.
overview_body: Each leaf runs on its own carriage and folds flat against the next, so an entire elevation gathers into a stack roughly the width of one panel. Nothing swings into the room and nothing is left standing in the middle of the opening.
The folding series take leaves up to 800 × 1600 mm inside an overall opening of 1500 × 2200 mm, at 45 kg a leaf and 150 kg of system capacity.

strengths.title: Folds to a stack
strengths.copy: The leaves gather at one jamb rather than sliding behind each other, so the opening is genuinely clear.

strengths.title: Flush thresholds
strengths.copy: The track can sit level with the finished floor — which matters most where a room runs straight out onto a terrace.

strengths.title: 45 kg a leaf
strengths.copy: Light enough to move in sequence with one hand, inside a system rated to 150 kg in total.

strengths.title: Sealed against weather
strengths.copy: Every leaf closes onto the same gasket line — Class 4 air permeability and 600 Pa of water tightness.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue, with the series that suit Bi-Fold listed first.
systems.teaser_desc: An entire elevation that folds away, panel by panel, until nothing stands between inside and out.
systems.enquiry_note: Panels fold and stack to one side, opening the whole wall to the outside.

variants.name: Six-Leaf Bi-Fold
variants.lede: Six leaves gather into a stack about one panel wide.

systems.name: Casement
systems.meta_description: Glaze casement aluminium windows and doors — concealed hinges, multi-point locking, leaves to 130 kg and 2.8 metres tall.
systems.schema_description: Aluminium casement windows and doors with concealed hinges, multi-point locking and leaves to 2.8 metres.
systems.hero_lede: Sashes that swing clear of the frame — every opening a whole opening.
overview_body: An outward-opening sash on concealed hinges clears the frame entirely, so the whole opening becomes airflow rather than a gap at the top. Multi-point locking then draws the leaf into a continuous gasket on every edge, not just beside the handle.
The casement family runs from a single window to a full-height double door, sharing the thermally broken core and the tested seal with every other Glaze system.

strengths.title: Concealed hinges
strengths.copy: Nothing breaks the line of the frame when the sash is shut, and nothing collects dirt where the two meet.

strengths.title: Multi-point locking
strengths.copy: Locking points run the full sash edge, so the gasket is compressed evenly rather than only at one point.

strengths.title: Leaves to 2.8 metres
strengths.copy: The 130 and 150 series carry a 2800 mm leaf at up to 130 kg — tall enough for full-height glazing.

strengths.title: Sealed against weather
strengths.copy: Class 4 air permeability and 600 Pa of water tightness with no leakage — tested to BS EN 12207 and 12208.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue, with the series that suit Casement listed first.
systems.teaser_desc: The refined classic — outward-opening sashes on concealed hinges, engineered for effortless ventilation and an uncompromising seal.
systems.enquiry_note: Hinged, outward-opening sashes — the classic for bedrooms, kitchens and studies.

systems.name: Tilt & Turn
systems.page_title: Tilt & Turn Systems — Glaze Window Systems
systems.meta_description: Glaze tilt and turn aluminium windows — one handle, two windows: tilt for background air, turn for the whole opening.
systems.schema_description: Aluminium tilt and turn window systems with dual-action hardware, inward opening and multi-point locking.
systems.hero_lede: A quarter turn tilts the head inward for air. A half turn opens the whole sash into the room.
overview_body: One handle drives two entirely different openings. At ninety degrees the sash tilts in at the head — background air, with the leaf still locked at every other point. At one hundred and eighty it swings fully inward, which is the whole opening, and which is also how you clean the outside of a window on the ninth floor from inside the room.

Because it opens inward, nothing swings out over a balcony, a walkway or a neighbouring elevation — the reason tilt and turn is the default across most of Europe, and the reason it belongs on tight urban sites here.

strengths.title: Two positions, one handle
strengths.copy: Tilt for air you can leave unattended, turn for the full opening. No second control, and nothing to learn.

strengths.title: Ventilate securely
strengths.copy: In the tilt position the leaf stays locked everywhere except the head — an opening nobody can reach through.

strengths.title: Cleaned from inside
strengths.copy: The sash swings fully into the room, so the outer face is reachable without a cradle or a ladder.

strengths.title: Nothing swings out
strengths.copy: Inward opening keeps the sash clear of balconies, walkways and boundary lines — and out of the wind.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue, with the series that suit Tilt & Turn listed first.
systems.teaser_desc: One handle, two windows. A quarter turn tilts the head inward for air; a half turn swings the whole sash into the room.
systems.enquiry_note: One handle, two positions — tilt for secure background air, turn for the whole opening.

variants.name: Single Tilt & Turn
variants.lede: One handle, two windows: a quarter turn tilts, a half turn swings.

systems.name: Pivot
systems.meta_description: Glaze pivot aluminium windows — oversized panels balanced on a single axis, sealed all round when closed.
systems.schema_description: Aluminium pivot window systems with oversized panels balanced on a single rotation axis.
systems.hero_lede: An oversized panel that turns on a single silent axis, in balance at every angle.
overview_body: The panel rotates about its own centre rather than hanging off one edge, so the load sits on the axis instead of the hinge side. That is what lets the format grow well past what a hinged sash would carry at the same frame depth.
Because it is balanced, a very large pane stays exactly where it is left — half open is a position, not something you have to hold.

strengths.title: Central-axis rotation
strengths.copy: The load sits on the axis, not on one edge, so the panel does not drop out of square over the years.

strengths.title: Oversized formats
strengths.copy: Panes far larger than a hinged sash could carry, in a frame that stays slim.

strengths.title: Stays where you leave it
strengths.copy: A balanced panel holds any angle without a stay or a catch.

strengths.title: Sealed all round
strengths.copy: Closed, the gasket runs unbroken around the full perimeter of the frame.

systems.teaser_desc: A statement in motion. Oversized panels that rotate on a single silent axis — perfectly balanced at every angle.
systems.enquiry_note: Turns on a central axis — a statement entrance door or feature window.

systems.name: Fixed
systems.meta_description: Glaze fixed aluminium windows — the thinnest possible frame around a permanent pane, with no moving parts at all.
systems.schema_description: Fixed aluminium window systems with minimal sightlines and no moving parts.
systems.hero_lede: No hinges, no rails, no motion — only the thinnest frame we can draw around a pane of glass.
overview_body: With nothing to open there is nothing to accommodate: no sash inside the frame, no hardware in the reveal, no clearance left for movement. What remains is very close to glass held in a line.
Fixed lights are usually specified alongside an opening system, taking the spans that never need to open so the operable panels can stay a sensible size.

strengths.title: Zero moving parts
strengths.copy: Nothing to wear, adjust or service — the assembly is the same in year twenty as on the day it was set.

strengths.title: Thinnest sightlines
strengths.copy: Without a sash inside the frame, the visible aluminium comes down to the structural minimum.

strengths.title: Maximum glass
strengths.copy: More of the opening is glazed than any operable system can manage at the same size.

strengths.title: Sealed permanently
strengths.copy: A continuous bond rather than a compression seal, so there is no gasket line to maintain.

systems.series_note: The full Glaze catalogue. Open a series to see its tested numbers.
systems.teaser_desc: Some views should never be interrupted. No hinges, no rails, no motion — only the thinnest possible frame around a perfect picture.
systems.enquiry_note: Pure glass with no moving parts — for light and views where nothing needs to open.
